content.title: About
content.content: Garlic bread is a fragrant slice of bread topped with a mixture of butter, minced garlic, herbs, and sometimes cheese. It is commonly served in fast‑food outlets and restaurants as an appetizer or side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first garlic‑bread recipe appeared in Italy in the early 1920s.
Garlic bread became popular in the United States in the 1970s thanks to chain pizzerias.
There is a “black” garlic bread version that incorporates cuttlefish ink into the dough.
Garlic bread is often served with marinara or cheese sauce for dipping.
Vegan versions replace butter with plant‑based margarine.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Garlic contains allicin and other compounds that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports immune function
items.content: Regular consumption of garlic may boost the body’s natural defenses.

items.title: May lower cholesterol
items.content: Studies suggest garlic can help reduce LDL (bad) cholesterol levels.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates and energy
items.content: The bread provides a quick source of energy through its carbs.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Bread supplies thiamine, niacin, and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Wheat allergy or gluten intolerance
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should avoid traditional garlic bread.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Butter and added salt make it fairly salty; those with hypertension should limit portions.

items.title: Gas and digestive discomfort
items.content: Garlic can cause bloating in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Butter and bread make the dish calorie‑rich, so moderation is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Garlic bread is usually served hot, cut into triangles. It can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, used for dipping into sauces, or as a side to soups, salads, and pasta dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a bag for up to 2 months. Reheat before serving and ensure the bread has not dried out.
